nutrient_numbers: DRAFT, NOT FOR APPROVAL YET: composition of Aminoven Infant 10% (100 g amino acids/l) from the Spanish SmPC, cross-checked value by value against the South African PI and the Swiss Fachinformation (all 18 amino acid values, total nitrogen 14.9 g/l and osmolarity 885 mosm/l agree). The Philippine registration DR-XY23408 is Aminosteril Infant 6% solution, so these per-liter values cannot be shown for the PH product until the concentration question is resolved.

registrations.packaging: Type I Glass Bottle x 100 mL

summary: Aminosteril Infant 6% (Fresenius Kabi Austria GmbH) is a pediatric amino acid solution, registered in the Philippines as 100 ml glass bottles.
composition_notes: Theoretical osmolarity 885 mosm/l; titratable acidity 25 to 45 mmol NaOH/l; pH 5.5 to 6.0 (Spanish SmPC section 2). Without electrolytes and carbohydrates; contains taurine (Fresenius Kabi MENA product page).
Energy in kJ differs between national texts (1675 kJ/l in the Spanish SmPC, 1680 kJ/l in the Swiss text); 400 kcal/l in both.

National-name substitute: Aminoven Infant 10% product information is used for Aminosteril Infant (same manufacturer); same formulation per Dr. Rivero (Nov 17 2026). The Philippine registration states a 6% solution, so concentration must be confirmed before these numbers apply.
dosing_limits: Continuous intravenous infusion through a central vein; maximum rate 0.1 g amino acids/kg/hour (1.0 ml/kg/hour) (Spanish SmPC 4.2, for the 10% solution).

Maximum daily dose (10% solution): age 1 year 1.5 to 2.5 g amino acids/kg (15 to 25 ml/kg); 2 to 5 years 1.5 g/kg (15 ml/kg); 6 to 14 years 1.0 g/kg (10 ml/kg) (Spanish SmPC 4.2; same in the South African PI). The Swiss text gives a preterm maximum of 2.5 g/kg/day.
kidney_notes: Spanish SmPC and South African PI: patients with renal or hepatic insufficiency require an individualized dose; frequent monitoring includes urea nitrogen, ammonia, electrolytes, glucose and triglycerides (SmPC 4.4).
Swiss Fachinformation: renal insufficiency and unknown kidney function are listed as contraindications. National texts differ; follow the Philippine package insert.
Renal amino acid losses with amino acid imbalance can occur if the infusion is too rapid or in overdose (South African PI 4.8, 4.9).
guideline_heading: How it fits the ESPEN 2021 kidney nutrition guideline
guideline: ESPEN 2021 Recommendation 24: "No disease-specific enteral nor parenteral formula oriented for patients with reduced kidney function should be routinely utilized in every patient with AKI, AKI on CKD, or CKD with KF in comparison to conventional formulas. Instead, their use is to be individualized (see recommendation 26)." Grade of recommendation B – Consensus (87.5% agreement).

ESPEN 2021 Recommendation 31: "Electrolytes abnormalities are common in patients with AKI, AKI on CKD, or CKD with KF receiving KRT and shall be closely monitored." Grade of recommendation A – Strong consensus (100% agreement).
bottom_line: A pediatric amino acid solution; the ESPEN 2021 kidney guideline quoted here covers hospitalized adults. Composition and SmPC text are pending the Philippine package insert.
withheld: Approval on hold: the Philippine registration (DR-XY23408) is Aminosteril Infant 6% solution, while the substitute source is Aminoven Infant 10%; per-liter composition and ml/kg doses do not transfer until the PH concentration and formulation are confirmed.
